relevance_reason: Reports individuals with biallelic ERI1 null variants who had mild intellectual disability and digital anomalies, and contrasts them with individuals carrying missense variants who had SEMD. This defines the phenotypic dichotomy relevant to this entry.

findings.statement: Guo et al. (2023) reported 8 affected individuals from 7 unrelated families with biallelic ERI1 variants and described a phenotypic dichotomy. Individuals with biallelic null variants had mild intellectual disability and digital anomalies, without the severe spondyloepimetaphyseal dysplasia (SEMD) seen in the 5 individuals with missense variants.
quotes: we uncover a phenotypic dichotomy associated with bi-allelic ERI1 variants by reporting eight affected individuals from seven unrelated families

A severe spondyloepimetaphyseal dysplasia (SEMD) was identified in five affected individuals with missense variants but not in those with bi-allelic null variants, who showed mild intellectual disability and digital anomalies.

findings.statement: Guo et al. (2023) identified biallelic null variants in the ERI1 gene in individuals with mild intellectual disability and digital anomalies. Biallelic missense variants were found in 5 individuals with severe SEMD.
quotes: A severe spondyloepimetaphyseal dysplasia (SEMD) was identified in five affected individuals with missense variants but not in those with bi-allelic null variants, who showed mild intellectual disability and digital anomalies.

findings.statement: Guo et al. (2023) proposed a model in which, within recessive ERI1 genotypes, missense alleles have a more severe effect than null alleles. Missense alleles caused severe SEMD, whereas null alleles caused a milder phenotype of mild intellectual disability and digital anomalies.
quotes: provides a model showing a more severe effect of missense alleles than null alleles within recessive genotypes

findings.statement: Guo et al. (2023) found that the ERI1 missense variants abolished exoribonuclease activity. This caused defective trimming of the 3-prime end of 5.8S rRNA and reduced degradation of replication-dependent histone mRNAs.
quotes: The ERI1 missense variants cause a loss of the exoribonuclease activity, leading to defective trimming of the 5.8S rRNA 3' end and a decreased degradation of replication-dependent histone mRNAs.

findings.statement: Guo et al. (2023) found that induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) derived from affected individuals showed impaired chondrogenesis in vitro, with downregulation of genes that regulate skeletal patterning.
quotes: Affected-individual-derived induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) showed impaired in vitro chondrogenesis with downregulation of genes regulating skeletal patterning.

relevance_reason: This is the first report of a patient with a homozygous ERI1 nonsense variant, and it defines the Hoxha-Aliu syndrome phenotype.

findings.statement: Hoxha and Aliu (2023) reported a female patient with mild intellectual disability, eyelid ptosis, and hand and foot anomalies. The hand and foot anomalies were brachydactyly, clinodactyly, dysplastic or short nails of the halluces, brachytelephalangy, short metacarpals, and toe syndactyly.
quotes: The patient exhibits mild intellectual disability, eyelid ptosis, and anomalies in her hands and feet (brachydactyly, clinodactyly, dysplastic/short nail of halluces, brachytelephalangy, short metacarpals, and toe syndactyly).

phenotypes.hpo_label: Shortening of all distal phalanges of the fingers

findings.statement: Hoxha and Aliu (2023) identified a homozygous nonsense variant in the ERI1 gene in a female patient with developmental delay and distal limb abnormalities. They described this as the first reported human case associated with ERI1 variants.
quotes: Here, we present a case of a female patient with a homozygous nonsense variant in ERI1 gene.
the pathology associated with ERI1 variants in humans has remained elusive because no case has been reported so far

findings.statement: Hoxha and Aliu (2023) described ERI1 as an evolutionarily conserved 3-prime-to-5-prime exonuclease that has an important function in multiple RNA processing pathways.
quotes: ERI1 is an evolutionary conserved 3'-5' exonuclease with an important function in multiple RNA processing pathways.

relevance_reason: The paper is mainly about Congenital NAD Deficiency Disorder (HAAO/KYNU). It is relevant here because it reports one patient (F5.II.1) with limb and cardiac defects who carries a homozygous loss-of-function ERI1 variant. The authors note that ERI1 was previously found in a homozygous microdeletion, together with MFHAS1, in a patient with similar limb and cardiac abnormalities.

findings.statement: Szot et al. (2021) found that patient F5.II.1, a girl with limb reduction defects, cardiac defects, microcephaly, global developmental delay, and autism, carried a homozygous loss-of-function variant in ERI1 (NM_153332.4: c.514C>T, p.Gln172Ter). She was also homozygous for a KYNU missense variant (c.616G>A, p.Glu206Lys). The authors noted that ERI1 had previously been found in a homozygous microdeletion, together with MFHAS1, in a patient whose limb and cardiac abnormalities resembled hers. They suggested that this additional variant may help explain her phenotype, but said the functional link between ERI1 mutation and these defects remained to be assessed.
quotes: F5.II.1 carries a homozygous LOF variant in NM_153332.4(ERI1):c.514C>T p.(Gln172*), a gene which has previously been identified in a homozygous microdeletion encompassing an additional gene MFHAS1 in a patient with similar limb and cardiac abnormalities to F5.II.1.

Whereas the functional link between ERI1 mutation and these defects remains to be assessed, the impact of these additional variants may confound the contribution of mild NAD deficiency observed in these two patients.
Both F5.II.1 and F6.II.4 harbor additional gene variants which may partially explain their distinct phenotypes, despite their suspected relatively mild NAD deficiency caused by KYNU mutation.

findings.statement: Szot et al. (2021) described a girl (F5.II.1) with reduction defects of the hands and feet. On the right hand she had a transverse terminal limb reduction with a rudimentary fifth digit. Several digits had hypoplastic or absent nails, toes 2 to 4 of the right foot and toes 3 to 5 of the left foot were absent, and there was syndactyly. She also had a perimembranous ventricular septal defect, pulmonary vein stenosis, microcephaly, global developmental delay, autism, brachycephaly with a flat occiput and bitemporal narrowing, a small nose, cupped prominent ears, and bilateral inguinal hernias. No vertebral or renal defects were recorded.
quotes: (KYNU) F5 | II.1 [c.616G>A; p.(Glu206Lys)]; [c.616G>A; p.(Glu206Lys)] | Female | - | Perimembranous ventricular septal defect, pulmonary vein stenosis | - |

Reduction defects (right hand transverse terminal limb reduction, rudimentary 5th digit; left hand hypoplastic deep set nails in digits 1/2,/3/ 5; right foot digits 1 + 5 have no nails; digits 2/3/4 absent; left foot digits 3/4/5 are absent (no bones), digits 1 + 2 have no nails, syndactyly)

Microcephaly, global developmental delay, autism, craniofacies (brachycephalic, flat occiput, bitemporal narrowing, normoteloric with normal eyebrows, small nose with a normal philtrum, ears cupped and prominent), bilateral inguinal hernias

phenotypes.text: transverse terminal limb reduction of right hand

relevance_reason: The paper reports a patient from a consanguineous family with a homozygous 8p23.1 deletion that removes ERI1 and has the features of the syndrome (intellectual disability, limb anomalies, cardiac malformation).

findings.statement: Choucair et al. (2017) reported a male child born to consanguineous parents. He had intellectual disability, short stature, dysmorphic facial features, synpolydactyly, and cardiac malformations.
quotes: A male child, born from consanguineous parents and having intellectual disability, short stature, dysmorphic facial features, synpolydactyly, and cardiac malformations is reported.

findings.statement: In a male child born to consanguineous parents, Choucair et al. (2017) used chromosomal microarray analysis and found a homozygous deletion at 8p23.1. The deletion contained the microRNA miR-4660 and the ERI1 and MFHAS1 genes. The authors noted that ERI1 is a ribonuclease involved in RNA metabolism and is required for correct skeletal patterning by defining HOXC8 expression. They discussed how the deleted genes might contribute to the patient's features.
quotes: Chromosomal microarray analysis showed that the patient presents with an 8p23.1 homozygous deletion, containing the microRNA miR-4660, the exoribonuclease 1 (ERI1), and malignant fibrous histiocytoma amplified sequence 1 (MFHAS1) genes.
ERI1 is a ribonuclease involved in RNA metabolism and is required for the correct patterning of the skeleton by defining the HOXC8 expression.

variants.as_reported: 8p23.1 homozygous deletion containing miR-4660, ERI1, and MFHAS1
